**Marcus k_RISC (high-T limit):**

$$k_{RISC} = \frac{2\pi}{\hbar} |H_{SOC}|^2 \frac{1}{\sqrt{4\pi \lambda k_B T}} \exp\left(-\frac{(\lambda + \Delta E_{ST})^2}{4\lambda k_B T}\right)$$

Note: ΔE_ST = E(S1) − E(T1) > 0, so for RISC (T1→S1) the activation term uses (λ + ΔE_ST)² since ΔG = +ΔE_ST.

Constants (SI then convert):
- ħ = 1.054571817 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s
- k_B = 1.380649 × 10⁻²³ J/K
- 1 cm⁻¹ = 1.986446 × 10⁻²³ J (energy), so H_SOC in J: 0.32 × 1.986446e-23 = 6.35663 × 10⁻²⁴ J
- |H_SOC|² = 4.04067 × 10⁻⁴⁷ J²
- 1 eV = 1.602177 × 10⁻¹⁹ J
- λ = 0.18 eV = 2.88392 × 10⁻²⁰ J
- ΔE_ST = 0.085 eV = 1.36185 × 10⁻²⁰ J
- k_B T at 298.15 K = 4.11635 × 10⁻²¹ J (= 0.025693 eV)

Prefactor: 2π/ħ × |H_SOC|² = (6.28319 / 1.054572e-34) × 4.04067e-47
= 5.95805e34 × 4.04067e-47 = 2.40745e-12 (units: J⁻¹·s⁻¹... wait, J²·(J·s)⁻¹ = J/s, then divide by √(J²)=J gives 1/s ✓)

Density-of-states factor: 1/√(4π λ k_B T)
- 4π λ k_B T = 12.5664 × 2.88392e-20 × 4.11635e-21 = 1.49186e-39 J²
- √ = 3.86246e-20 J
- 1/√ = 2.58902e19 J⁻¹

Activation: (λ + ΔE_ST)² / (4 λ k_B T)
- λ + ΔE_ST = 0.265 eV = 4.24577e-20 J
- (λ + ΔE_ST)² = 1.80266e-39 J²
- 4 λ k_B T = 4.74803e-40 J²
- ratio = 3.79665
- exp(−3.79665) = 0.022430

k_RISC = 2.40745e-12 × 2.58902e19 × 0.022430
= 6.23292e7 × 0.022430
= 1.398e6 s⁻¹

$$k_F (s^{-1}) = 2.88 \times 10^{-9} \cdot n^2 \cdot f \cdot \langle \tilde\nu^{-3}\rangle^{-1}_{avg} \approx 0.667 \cdot f \cdot \tilde\nu^2$$
